intro: Answer each of the twelve signs for your own website — Yes (this is true of my site), No (this is not true of my site), or Unsure (I have not actually checked). Nothing is pre-filled and nothing defaults to Yes or No: an honest starting point is that you have not tested most of this on a real phone yet. The result sorts what you find into what is actually costing you sales right now, what is quietly compounding, and what is genuinely cosmetic.

tiers.label: Revenue-blocking — can end a sale outright
tiers.urgencyNote: Each of these can stop a single visitor from becoming a customer in one visit, with no error message telling you it happened. Three or more present is a strong signal that a redesign conversation is already overdue.

items.label: Mobile friction
items.shortDescription: Phone number not tappable, form fields awkward to fill, menu or pop-up covering the main action on a phone screen.
items.businessCostMechanism: More than half of most Swiss SME traffic now arrives on mobile at the moment of highest intent. Friction here turns a ready buyer into someone who closes the tab meaning to return on a laptop, and typically does not.
items.testHint: Open the site on your own phone, on mobile data (not office Wi-Fi), and try to complete the one action you most want a visitor to take.

items.label: Slow load speed on mobile
items.shortDescription: The site takes noticeably longer to become usable on a phone than it does on the office computer.
items.businessCostMechanism: Speed cost falls almost entirely on new-customer acquisition: a visitor with no existing relationship to the business has the least patience and the most alternatives one tap away.
items.testHint: Time how long it takes from tapping a search result to being able to actually read or tap something, on mobile data, not Wi-Fi.

items.label: Broken or unreliable contact/enquiry forms
items.shortDescription: A form that may fail silently — no confirmation message, no email arriving, no error shown to the visitor.
items.businessCostMechanism: Produces zero symptoms visible to the business. No bounce, no complaint — the visitor believes contact was made; the business believes it simply received no enquiries.
items.testHint: Submit the form yourself from a phone, on mobile data, and confirm the notification email actually arrives — do this quarterly, not once.

items.label: No clear call to action
items.shortDescription: Pages explain the business but never tell the visitor what to do next, or bury the instruction below the fold.
items.businessCostMechanism: A visitor who has to invent their own next step usually just leaves once the information is absorbed, assuming the business would have said what to do if there were something to do.
items.testHint: Load your busiest page and time how long it takes to find one specific instruction telling you what to do next.

items.label: Expired SSL certificate or a visible browser security warning
items.shortDescription: Browser shows "Not secure", a certificate warning, or a broken-padlock icon on any page.
items.businessCostMechanism: Ends the visit before a single word of the page is read. The browser has already made the trust decision for the visitor, and it is not one most people know how to argue with.
items.testHint: Open the site in an incognito/private window and check the address bar for any warning, on both the homepage and at least one inner page.

tiers.label: Compounding — erodes results without a single visible failure
tiers.urgencyNote: These rarely stop one sale outright. Their cost is gradual and invisible until measured across a few quarters — worth fixing within a quarter, not necessarily this week.

items.label: Unclear offer or value proposition
items.shortDescription: A first-time visitor cannot tell within the first screen what the business does, who it is for, and why it is a reasonable choice.
items.businessCostMechanism: Visitors who are not told they are the right kind of customer do not self-select into becoming an enquiry — like a shop with an unmarked door losing exactly the footfall the sign would have captured.
items.testHint: Show the homepage to someone unfamiliar with the business for ten seconds and ask them to say back what it does and who it is for.

items.label: Weak trust signals
items.shortDescription: No physical address, no register/association reference, a phone number with the wrong country code, no evidence real people work there.
items.businessCostMechanism: At the point of contact, the real decision is trust, not need. Each missing signal removes one small reason to proceed at the moment hesitation is most expensive.
items.testHint: List what a stranger could verify about the business from the site alone, without searching elsewhere.

items.label: No working analytics tracking
items.shortDescription: GA4 or an equivalent is missing, broken, or was never actually verified to be recording real visits.
items.businessCostMechanism: Without measurement, none of the other eleven signs can be checked in real numbers — only guessed at from memory and mood.
items.testHint: Open the analytics dashboard right now and confirm it shows visits from today, not just a historical baseline.

items.label: Indexing or technical SEO problems
items.shortDescription: Pages missing from Google search results, a leftover noindex tag, duplicate page titles, or no submitted sitemap.
items.businessCostMechanism: Costs sales among visitors who never arrive at all — the only sign on this list with no visitor experience to notice, because there was no visit.
items.testHint: Search Google for the exact business name plus one core service and confirm the right page appears.

tiers.label: Operational — costs your team more than a single sale
tiers.urgencyNote: Real, but the most cosmetic of the twelve. Worth fixing, but after the nine above, not instead of them.

items.label: Outdated technical ownership — cannot be edited or updated
items.shortDescription: Nobody at the business has working login access to the site's code, hosting account, or domain registrar.
items.businessCostMechanism: Rarely costs a sale on an ordinary day. Becomes expensive the day something urgent needs changing and nobody can reach whoever holds the credentials.
items.testHint: Confirm someone at the business can currently log in to the hosting account and the domain registrar, today, without contacting a third party.

items.label: Difficult content-editing workflow
items.shortDescription: A one-line text change requires a developer, a support ticket, or a wait of several days.
items.businessCostMechanism: Small edits that should take minutes simply do not get made — a stale opening-hours notice or an expired promotion left live is a small, avoidable reason to doubt the business is paying attention.
items.testHint: Time how long it actually took the last time something small on the site needed changing.

items.label: Inconsistent branding
items.shortDescription: Logo, colours or tone differ between the website, invoices, and the Google Business Profile.
items.businessCostMechanism: Registers with professional buyers as evidence of how carefully the business runs its other processes — real, but nobody has ever failed to submit a form over a shade of blue.
items.testHint: Open the website, a recent invoice, and the Google Business Profile side by side and compare the logo and colours.

gapLogic.description: Each item has three possible states: yes (sign present), no (sign absent), unsure (not actually checked). Nothing defaults to yes or no. The tool never produces a single blended percentage score across all twelve items, because one revenue-blocking 'yes' matters more than three operational 'yes' answers combined — an average would hide exactly the distinction this tool exists to make. Instead it counts 'yes' answers within each tier separately and reads the three counts through summaryRules, then lists every 'yes' item as a prioritized worklist (revenue-blocking first, then compounding, then operational) and every 'unsure' item as a separate 'test this before deciding' list.

summaryRules.message: Three or more revenue-blocking signs are present. A redesign conversation is already overdue — patching each individually will likely cost more in total than planning the fix as one project.
One or two revenue-blocking signs plus several compounding signs. Targeted fixes now — the specific items listed below — may reasonably buy a year or two before a full redesign earns its cost.
One or two revenue-blocking signs, without much compounding damage yet. Fix these specific items directly — this does not look like a full-redesign case on its own.
No sign here can end a sale outright, but several compounding signs are quietly eroding results. Worth fixing within the quarter, and worth measuring rather than guessing at from here on.
Only operational signs are present. This is a maintenance and process conversation, not yet a redesign business case.
No sign confirmed present, but some items were marked unsure. Test those specific items on a real phone before concluding the site has no revenue-blocking problems.

None of the twelve signs are present. If sales still feel weak, the cause is more likely traffic volume or positioning than the website itself — worth diagnosing separately before spending on a redesign.

outputSections.label: Prioritized worklist
outputSections.description: Every item marked 'yes', ordered tier first (revenue-blocking, then compounding, then operational), each shown with its businessCostMechanism text — this is the 'actually costing you money' list, in order.

outputSections.label: Test these before deciding
outputSections.description: Every item marked 'unsure', shown with its testHint — a short, specific action to turn a guess into a yes or no.

outputSections.label: Cosmetic — real, but can wait
outputSections.description: Any operational-tier item marked 'yes', shown separately even though it also appears in the worklist, so it is never mistaken for equally urgent to a revenue-blocking item.

disclaimer: All answers in this tool come from you and are processed only in your browser — no real website is scanned automatically, and nothing you enter is transmitted or stored. This produces a prioritized starting point for a conversation, not a technical audit, a guaranteed sales figure, or a guaranteed ranking outcome. No result from this tool constitutes SEO, legal or accessibility certification.
